extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of humor, communication scholars, psychologists, and general readers interested in humor
extracted.subtask_description: Frameworks and topics for analyzing humor across media, society, and psyche, including techniques, joke morphology, cultural/ethnic dimensions, literary and visual examples, and therapeutic/creative functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor, psyche, and society
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor permeates every aspect of society and relates to psychological and social life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of jokes a person enjoys contribute significantly to the definition of that person and to the character of a given society; social researchers should analyze how humor functions across daily media (television, newspapers, literature) and interpersonal contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary of techniques of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: A catalogue/glossary of the techniques that generate humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides definitions and examples of specific comedic techniques (from simple puns to more elaborate devices) so analysts can identify which technique a text or performance uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphology of the joke/tale
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural analysis of jokes and humorous tales—their parts and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines how jokes are constructed (e.g., setup, misdirection, punch line) and how tale morphology shapes comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy of a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed breakdown of what constitutes a joke at the micro level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on elements such as timing, wording, incongruity, and the mechanics that produce the laugh; useful for both critique and creation of jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnic and racial jokes in social context
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of ethnic and racial jokes and their relation to American society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers examples (e.g., 'The Telephone Pole with the Braided Armpits') and how such jokes reflect, reinforce, or critique social attitudes and power relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of culturally specific jokes (Jewish jokes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Close readings of culturally specific jokes with implications for broader social questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'On Me You Cant Count' — interprets a Jewish joke with relevance to the 'Jewish Question'; shows how particular jokes illuminate group identity, stereotype, and self-definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jewish fools and comedic figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Study of recurring comic figures in a tradition (e.g., 'Jewish fools' from Chelm to modern comedians).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks historical and cultural continuities in archetypal comic roles and what they reveal about communities and humor norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartoons and literary parity (Mickey Mouse and Krazy Kat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argues that cartoons and comic strips can contain as much complexity and ambiguity as major literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages reading visual popular culture (Mickey Mouse, Krazy Kat) with the same critical tools applied to novels like Huckleberry Finn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comics and popular culture (not just kids' stuff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of comics as a serious site of cultural meaning and humor production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyzes how comic strips, graphic narratives, and related media function humorously within popular culture and contribute to adult discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic techniques in drama (Twelfth Night)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of comedic technique analysis to dramatic works and social considerations in performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines how plays (e.g., Twelfth Night) employ comedic devices and how social context shapes their comic interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurdism and literary humor (Huckleberry Finn)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting novels as vehicles of absurd or existential humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Huckleberry Finn as an example of a 'novel of the absurd' and shows methods for making sense of an existential hero through a humor lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Healing with humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Explores the therapeutic and health-related effects of laughter and humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that 'a laugh a day keeps the doctor away'—reviews how humor benefits physical and mental health and how it can be used in therapeutic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy and creation (generative power of humor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation of how humor contributes to creativity and the generative processes of art and thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the role of humor in creative production, idea generation, and the broader creative process.
